site.name: tessera
site.summary: Tessera Fictional embedded SQL database official docs and function reference (PostgreSQL / DuckDB official-docs style). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Hero (title + slogan + Get started button + real syntax-highlighted SELECT SQL example); version switcher (v2.4 / v2.3 / v2.2 / v2.1); ⌘K search; three quick-start cards (Install / Connect / Your first query); 6 docs-section cards (Architecture / SQL Syntax / Functions / Data Types / Storage / Extensions); dark / light theme toggle. - `reference.html` — Reference main entry. **Three-column layout**: left deep TOC tree (Schemas / Tables / Views / Indexes / Functions [Aggregate / String / Numeric / Date-Time / JSON / Window sub-groups] / Operators [category sub-groups], nodes expandable / collapsible); center reference overview + popular links + v2.4 new-features callout; right-side on-this-page outline. - `function-date-trunc.html` — DATE_TRUNC function detail page (**canonical example spec**). Three-column layout; signature code block; parameter table; return value; 3 SQL examples with result tables (basic usage / GROUP BY pairing / nested EXTRACT); error-case callouts; collapsible version-history panel (added v1.0, microsecond un

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full tessera system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The exploration covered core documentation pages, reference layouts, and mobile responsiveness across the Tessera site. However, overall interactive feature coverage remains low (11%), leaving many specific reference links and data types untested. Significant UX friction stems from widespread placeholder links, a buggy sidebar active state, broken scrollspy navigation, and horizontal overflow issues on mobile viewports caused by unconstrained data tables.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and validate the UX of the Tessera documentation site, focusing on navigation, global controls, reference layout, and responsive design.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will first validate the homepage global controls like the version switcher, search modal, and theme toggle. It will then traverse the main reference documentation, verifying the deep left-side TOC and right-side page outlines. After examining specific content types like functions and operators, the run will conclude with mobile viewport checks to assess the impact of flagged small tap targets and the responsive behavior of the complex 3-column layouts.
assumptions: The ⌘K search button triggers a modal or search overlay.
The left TOC on reference pages contains expandable/collapsible sections.
Function pages like DATE_TRUNC have collapsible version history panels.
The site uses a responsive design that collapses the 3-column layout on smaller viewports.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets for header navigation and global controls (Search, Theme, Version).
Missing accessible label on the version switcher <select>.
Usability of the deep left-side TOC on mobile devices.
Collapsible panels (TOC nodes, version history) state management.

phases.title: Homepage & Global Controls
phases.objective: Verify the functionality of global header controls and homepage links.
key_checks: Toggle the dark/light theme (🌓 button) and verify visual change.
Interact with the version switcher (<select>) and check for accessibility issues.
Click '⌘ K Search' and verify if a search interface appears.
Test primary call-to-action buttons ('Get started', 'View reference').
exit_criteria: Global header controls have been interacted with and their states/UI changes recorded.

phases.title: Reference Structure & TOC
phases.objective: Validate the 3-column documentation layout and internal navigation mechanisms.
key_checks: Navigate using the left-hand Table of Contents.
Expand and collapse nodes within the left TOC (Schemas, Tables, Functions, etc.).
Click links in the right-side 'On this page' outline to verify smooth scrolling or anchor navigation.
exit_criteria: Left TOC expand/collapse functionality and right-side anchor links have been exercised.

phases.title: Content Pages & Interactions
phases.objective: Examine specific reference pages for layout integrity and interactive components.
key_checks: Verify readability of large tables (e.g., Data types, Operators).
Check syntax highlighting and layout of SQL code blocks and result tables.
Interact with the 'Version history' collapsible panel on the DATE_TRUNC page.
Verify external links like 'Edit this page on GitHub'.
exit_criteria: Various content types (tables, code blocks) and page-specific interactions have been validated.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Assess the usability of the documentation on smaller screens, addressing layout warnings.
key_checks: Evaluate the usability of header navigation given the 'small_tap_target' warnings.
Verify how the 3-column layout on function pages collapses (e.g., does TOC become a hamburger menu?).
Check if wide data tables and code blocks scroll horizontally or break layout.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout adaptations and tap target usability have been documented.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit home, main reference, at least two category pages, and at least two function pages.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise search, theme toggle, version select, TOC expand/collapse, and page-specific toggles.
coverage_targets.mobile: Validate navigation, layout collapsing, and table/code block overflowing on mobile.

notes: Pay special attention to the 'Missing input label' warning on the version select dropdown and document the exact HTML implementation.

findings.user_goal: Read documentation and reference tables on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Content horizontally overflows the mobile viewport, forcing users to pan left and right to read.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings and trajectory notes indicate the page width reaches 439px on a 390px viewport on `function-date-trunc.html`, primarily caused by the 'Parameters' table where the 'Description' column is cut off and does not wrap properly.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal scrolling on mobile breaks the reading experience, making dense technical documentation difficult to consume and potentially causing users to miss crucial parameter details.
findings.suggestion: Implement responsive table wrappers with `overflow-x: auto` for data tables, or stack table columns vertically on small viewports.

findings.user_goal: Navigate to specific functions, tutorials, or onboarding guides.
findings.problem: Many prominent navigation elements and primary calls-to-action are dead placeholder links.
findings.evidence: The 'Get started' CTA on the homepage, top navigation links ('Tutorials', 'Download', 'GitHub'), and numerous sidebar function links (e.g., 'NOW', 'AVG', 'COUNT') use `href="#"` and fail to navigate anywhere.
findings.why_it_matters: Users rely on these links to learn the product. Encountering dead ends immediately erodes trust and prevents users from completing their primary onboarding or research goals.
findings.suggestion: Remove placeholder links from the UI if the content is not yet ready, or replace them with 'Coming Soon' states. Ensure all primary CTAs lead to functional pages.

findings.user_goal: Understand current location within the broader documentation structure.
findings.problem: The left sidebar's active state indicator frequently highlights the wrong page or multiple pages simultaneously.
findings.evidence: When viewing the SELECT statement page (`sql-select.html`), the sidebar incorrectly highlights `REGEXP_MATCH`. Cross-page navigation to `operators.html#comp` incorrectly highlights `LOWER`. Clicking placeholder links also visually highlights them without actually changing the page context.
findings.why_it_matters: Inconsistent or false active states disorient users, making it hard to mentally map the documentation structure or retrace their steps.
findings.suggestion: Fix the active state logic to accurately reflect the current window URL path and hash, and prevent placeholder links from triggering an active state change unless navigation actually occurs.

findings.user_goal: Track reading progress and jump between sections of a long reference page.
findings.problem: The right-hand 'ON THIS PAGE' outline tracker fails to update as the user scrolls down on most pages.
findings.evidence: On `data-types.html` and `function-json-extract.html`, the scrollspy logic is broken; the highlight remains stuck on the top item (e.g., 'Numeric' or 'Signature') even when the user has scrolled down to view the 'Composite' or 'Examples' sections.
findings.why_it_matters: Without dynamic feedback, the right-hand TOC loses its utility as a navigational aid, leaving users unsure of which sub-section they are currently reading.
findings.suggestion: Implement or fix the IntersectionObserver or scroll event listener logic that drives the scrollspy active state for the right-hand outline.

findings.user_goal: Search for specific documentation on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The mobile search modal has poor layout formatting, making results hard to scan.
findings.evidence: Trajectory notes indicate that when filtering search results in the mobile modal, items (like 'DATE_TRUNC' and 'DATE_ADD') display horizontally inline rather than stacking vertically, and long quick-link texts awkwardly wrap.
findings.why_it_matters: An inline horizontal layout for search results is non-standard and makes scanning a list of functions on a narrow screen very difficult.
findings.suggestion: Ensure search result items and quick links use `display: flex; flex-direction: column` or `display: block` on mobile viewports so they stack neatly in a vertical list.

findings.user_goal: Switch documentation versions to match the database version being used.
findings.problem: The version switcher dropdown is non-functional.
findings.evidence: Selecting 'v2.3' from the version dropdown updates the input value but does not trigger a page reload, navigation, or any visible content update (observed on both desktop and mobile).
findings.why_it_matters: Users relying on older versions of the software will be misled into thinking they are viewing accurate documentation for their version, potentially causing integration errors.
findings.suggestion: Wire the version switcher `<select>` to trigger a navigation event to the corresponding versioned URL when the `onchange` event fires.

findings.user_goal: Interact with UI controls like copying code or switching themes on mobile.
findings.problem: Several interactive elements have touch targets that are too small for comfortable mobile use.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings show the theme toggle is 40x32px, the 'Copy' buttons in code blocks are 48x22px, and the 'Edit this page on GitHub' link is 144x18px—all below the recommended 44x44px mobile minimum.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets increase the likelihood of misclicks or frustrating interactions for mobile users.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding or minimum height of these interactive elements to ensure a touch target of at least 44x44px on mobile devices.
findings.source_hint: Theme toggle, Copy buttons, GitHub link

findings.user_goal: Understand the purpose of a form control using a screen reader.
findings.problem: The version selector dropdown lacks an accessible label.
findings.evidence: The layout warnings flag a missing input label for the `<select>` element (id: ux-2) used for switching versions (v2.4, v2.3, etc.).
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users may not have enough context to understand what the dropdown controls without a clear programmatically associated label.
findings.suggestion: Add an `aria-label="Select documentation version"` or a visually hidden `<label>` associated with the `<select>` element.

gaps: Only directly exercised 11% of visible interactive feature signatures.
